html:
Coffee became Rwanda's main export after Belgian officials made peasant farmers grow it from the 1930s, and it remained the country's chief source of foreign money for decades.

Each household had to plant coffee trees, and the crop paid the taxes of the colonial state. After independence, small farmers kept growing it on the hills of the south and west, and the state bought it at fixed prices.

When world coffee prices collapsed in 1989, rural incomes and state revenue fell sharply, deepening the crisis under Habyarimana. After 1994 Rwanda rebuilt the trade around washing stations and high quality beans for buyers abroad. Tea and tourism have since joined coffee as earners.
sum: Coffee became Rwanda's main export after Belgian officials made peasant farmers grow it from the 1930s, and it remained the country's chief source of foreign money for decades.
